newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks weaken, despite banks rally.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks weaken, despite banks rally.

text.p: 10yrbond futs 91.885 +0.025 Gold NY 351.55 Lon fix 352.00
*Stocks end weaker despite a late rally in bank and BHP shares. Vol 324.61 million, value A$1,139.1 million, 1,086 stocks traded, 337 steady, 321 up, 428 down.
Australian stocks end weaker after swinging around all day on rumours of bank takeovers, the digestion of market bellwhether BHP result and in anticipation of a hike in U.S. interest rates.
At 4.25 p.m. (0525 GMT), the All Ordinaries index ended 4.9 points lower at 2,386.4. The March share price index futures shed 11 points to 2364 creating a 22.4 point discount to the physical market.
Brokers said an afternoon rally in bank shares and BHP lifted the market off its intra-day low of 2,378.8. Banks rose on a mixture of takeover talk and earnings upgrades.
"People are speculating about takeovers of banks and insurance companies," said Greg Matthews, executive director of equities at fund managers Mercantile Mutual.
Anti-monopolies watchdog ACCC chairman Allan Fels said this afternoon that there would be few competition concerns with a merger of a large bank and insurance company.
Matthews said both Westpac and ANZ rose on the back of earnings upgrade by banking analysts.
Both ANZ and Westpac ended about three percent higher, while the remaining two banks of Australia's big four Commonwealth Bank and NAB were slightly off.
Shares in BHP swung around most of the day after it released a 69.5 percent rise in third quarter profit, but analysts said the result was not as good as it appeared.
"Initially it (BHP) was okay, so people bid it up and then people looked at the quality of it and said it was poor and they sold it down and then it rallied again," Matthews said.

The market was weakened by continued selling of shares in media giant News Corp, which has fallen nearly 10 percent this week as investors dumped the stock in reaction to Rupert Murdoch's plans to issue more shares for acquisitions.
Tobacco stocks slumped following the settlement by U.S. tobacco group Liggett Group Inc, which admitted that nicotine is additive, the first admission of its kind.
W.D. & H.O. Wills fell over eight percent, while Rothmans was over seven percent lighter.
Brokers said the market has been edgy all week as there is increasing speculation U.S. interest rates may rise after Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting.
Falls outnumbered by a ratio of four to three while about 31 percent of stocks traded were steady. The media and chemical sectors were amongst the biggest fallers amongst the indices.
In other local markets, Australian bonds succumbed to a more subdued session with the reaction to a possible 25 basis point hike in U.S. interest rates now seen priced in for the FOMC meet.
By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 8.05 percent.
The Australian dollar stayed around its three-week levels.
By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), the Australian dollar was US$0.7838/43 just up from $0.7834/39 at the midsession.
